chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd from Muhammad ibn al-Ḥasan from Muhammad ibn Yaḥyā from Muhammad ibn al-Ḥusayn from Muhammad ibn Ismāʿīl from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah from Bashīr al-Dahhān who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Bashīr, indeed when the believer visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of ʿArafah, and performs ritual bath in the Euphrates, then turns towards it, Allah writes for him, with every step, a pilgrimage with all its rituals.' And I do not know him except to have said, 'and a military expedition.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husayn's grave on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the unique status of Karbala as a spiritual axis, linking the martyrdom of Imam al-Ḥusayn (AS) with the culmination of prophetic revelation on the Day of ʿArafah. The reward of a complete *hajj* and *ghazwah* for each step signifies that this visitation serves as a comprehensive act of worship, merging the devotion of pilgrimage with the sacrifice of military struggle. This elevates the shrine not merely as a memorial, but as a locus of divine acceptance where the believer’s physical journey translates into immense spiritual merit.
